newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Last two hostages in Indonesia's Irian found dead.
newsitem.headline: Last two hostages in Indonesia's Irian found dead.

text.p: Two forestry workers kidnapped in Indonesia's remote Irian Jaya province were found dead on Wednesday, ending a month-long hostage drama, the official Antara news agency reported.
Antara quoted the province's military spokesman, Lieutenant Colonel Maulud Hidayat, as saying a military search team found the two men, who were identified as Tumaji, 19, and Maksum, 28.
"They were tortured, tied up, then killed and thrown into a gorge," Hidayat was quoted as saying. The report said their bodies had been repeatedly stabbed.

The two were the last of a group of 12 people kidnapped on August 14 from a camp of forestry concessionaire PT Kamundan Jaya, which is part of the private agro-forestry Djanjanti Group. The camp was about 60 km (37 miles) from the mining town of Timika.
Local military authorities have since suspended logging in the district.

While the kidnappers were initially described as bandits seeking an end to logging by the company, the military has since described them as a "security disturbing group," the term it uses for the separtist Free Papua Movement (OPM).
In May, nine hostages, including six Europeans, were freed by a military operation after more than four months in OPM captivity. Two Indonesian hostages were killed by their captors.
Indonesia faces scattered resistance to its rule in Irian Jaya, a former Dutch colony it took control of in 1963, especially from the OPM.
